record.original_question: Is it true that the extension of the A. Agrachev–R. Gamkrelidze construction of groups from pre-Lie rings in(J. Soviet Math., 17(1981), 1650–1675) suggested in Definition 66 of(A. Smoktunowicz, J. Pure Appl. Algebra, 229, no. 12(2025), 108128) produces groups from pre-Lie rings? If this extended construction does give a group, then it also gives a brace, and so an affirmative answer to this question would have consequences for the theory of set-theoretic solutions of the Yang–Baxter equation and for the theory of braces.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(A,+,\cdot)$ be a pre-Lie ring; that is, $(A,+)$ is an abelian group equipped with a binary operation $\cdot$ satisfying the left pre-Lie identity
$$(a\cdot b)\cdot c - a\cdot(b\cdot c) = (b\cdot a)\cdot c - b\cdot(a\cdot c)\qquad(a,b,c\in A).$$
The classical construction of A. Agrachev and R. Gamkrelidze associates to a suitable (e.g. nilpotent, or formally completed) pre-Lie ring $A$ a group structure on the underlying set by means of a "group of flows" formula: one defines a binary operation $\ast$ on $A$ via a formal series in the pre-Lie product (a pre-Lie analogue of the Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff formula) that turns $(A,\ast)$ into a group whose multiplication can be expressed using only the operation $\cdot$.

Consider the following extension of this construction (the analogue of "Definition 66" in the setting referred to): given a pre-Lie ring $A$ (not assumed to be nilpotent or to lie in a complete topological setting), define a binary operation $\ast$ on $A$ by the same formal pre-Lie BCH-type expression, interpreted via the prescribed extension procedure that allows the formula to be evaluated on arbitrary pre-Lie rings.

Question: Does this extended construction always yield a group $(A,\ast)$ from any pre-Lie ring $A$? 

(If the answer is affirmative, then the resulting structure together with the addition of $A$ also forms a brace, with consequences for the theory of set-theoretic solutions of the Yang–Baxter equation and for the theory of braces. Recall that a left brace is a triple $(B,+,\circ)$ where $(B,+)$ is an abelian group, $(B,\circ)$ is a group, and $a\circ(b+c)+a = a\circ b + a\circ c$ for all $a,b,c\in B$.)
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears in the latest collection of new problems in the Kourovka Notebook (2026), suggesting it is currently open. Recent work by Smoktunowicz and collaborators (e.g., arXiv:2410.05924, 2208.02535, 2202.00085) studies the passage between pre-Lie rings and braces beyond the strongly nilpotent / Lazard regime, but no source verifies that the proposed extension of the Agrachev–Gamkrelidze construction yields a group on arbitrary pre-Lie rings.

status_evidence.title: On pre-Lie rings related to some non-Lazard braces
status_evidence.snippet: Recent paper by Smoktunowicz studying connections between pre-Lie rings and braces in non-Lazard settings.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research on extending the pre-Lie ring/brace correspondence beyond the classical (Lazard / strongly nilpotent) setting indicates the general extension is not settled.

status_evidence.title: From pre-Lie rings back to braces
status_evidence.snippet: Smoktunowicz constructs braces from pre-Lie rings under nilpotency hypotheses, leaving the general case open.
status_evidence.claim: Existing results pass from pre-Lie rings to braces only under restrictive hypotheses, so the question of whether the extended construction always yields a group remains open.
